headline: High: ms-swift can read/write local files and egress to model APIs, creating default data-leak and cascading-error risk when paired with Chatwoot support data.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot handles customer messages and reports, while ms-swift can read files and process stdin/stdout plus API-backed workflows. If Chatwoot content is passed into ms-swift as prompts or files, attacker-controlled support text could steer downstream instructions. The bridge is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Chatwoot conversation text is exported into ms-swift prompts or files, injection is possible.
IF the operator manually copies support content into ms-swift without sanitization, prompt hijacking can occur.
mitigations: Strip instructions from imported support text before passing it onward.
Use a fixed prompt template that quotes Chatwoot content as data only.
Review ms-swift inputs for embedded tool directives before execution.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags between Chatwoot exports and ms-swift inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, orders, messages, and reports; ms-swift handles files, logs, configuration, and secrets like hub_token/sdk-token, and can egress to external model APIs. If Chatwoot data is routed into ms-swift, sensitive support content can leave the local boundary through allowlisted network calls. The pairwise path is inferred from documented surfaces, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF Chatwoot customer records are exported into ms-swift training, evaluation, or logging paths, leakage occurs.
IF ms-swift sends imported content to ModelScope, HuggingFace, or OpenAI interfaces, data leaves the support system boundary.
mitigations: Disable outbound API calls for any job that ingests Chatwoot data.
Redact customer identifiers before export to ms-swift.
Keep Chatwoot exports in a separate workspace from model artifacts.
Rotate any hub_token or sdk-token used in the same session.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP checks on all ms-swift upload paths.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot is a support system with broad network egress, while ms-swift can execute shell commands, install packages, read/write the filesystem, and spawn subprocesses. If both are pointed at the same workspace or shared artifacts, they can overwrite each other's files or configs. Chatwoot lacks explicit write controls, but ms-swift's write surface makes the conflict plausible in default operator setups.
conditions: IF both agents share a writable directory for exports, configs, or logs, file clobbering can occur.
IF Chatwoot-generated artifacts are edited by ms-swift in place, concurrent state corruption is possible.
mitigations: Place each agent in its own directory.
Use read-only mounts for Chatwoot exports.
Avoid in-place edits of shared config files.
Snapshot files before ms-swift runs.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared workspace.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot produces customer-support content and reports, and ms-swift can consume files or stdin/stdout and then act through model APIs or evaluation pipelines. If ms-swift treats Chatwoot output as authoritative, a mistaken summary or hallucinated fact can cascade into downstream actions or model artifacts. Because no verification step is documented, the safer high severity is chosen.
conditions: IF Chatwoot output is fed into ms-swift without a verification step, errors can propagate.
IF ms-swift-generated summaries are reused as source-of-truth for support actions, cascading mistakes occur.
mitigations: Require human review before reusing ms-swift outputs.
Compare ms-swift summaries against original Chatwoot records.
Mark generated outputs as non-authoritative in filenames.
Limit ms-swift to read-only analysis of Chatwoot exports.
requires-engineering: add validation gates before any downstream action.

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot processes customer data and messages, while ms-swift handles datasets, logs, checkpoints, and secrets and can send content to external model services. That creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch if support data is exported into training or evaluation workflows. The profiles do not state HIPAA/GDPR specifics, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF customer support data is copied into ms-swift logs, checkpoints, or datasets, retention policy mismatch occurs.
IF exported Chatwoot data is sent to third-party model APIs, residency or processor terms may diverge.
mitigations: Exclude customer data from training datasets.
Set short retention on ms-swift logs and checkpoints.
Document which support fields may be exported.
Pseudonymize records before model workflows.
requires-engineering: align DPA and retention controls across both systems.
